absent: Definition and behavior of alloc tag save and restore used by hook wrappers.
Layout of code tag and code tag reference, meaning of generic tag initializer and inaccurate flag, and identity of shared counter holder.
How alloc tag sections are enumerated at runtime and how module section addresses and sizes are populated.
Behavior of early page frame accounting beyond the empty hook signature.
Full per CPU reference lifecycle including kill, mode switching, and release callback registration.
Writeback work scheduling, delayed work handlers, bandwidth update algorithm, and dirty throttling calculations.
Definition of device creator and lookup helpers for inode to device mapping and tree access.
Identity and values of memory and IO controller identifiers, superblock flags, and remaining device capability bits.
Lock ordering between list and work guards, interrupt context rules, and reference release paths for device info.
Exact numeric bit positions for writeback state and trigger reason enumerations.
Boot, ring, capability, and game state phase mapping anchors for these memory interfaces.

findings.text: Each header uses a single inclusion guard. First guard is _LINUX_ALLOC_TAG_H. Second guard is __LINUX_BACKING_DEV_DEFS_H. Third guard is _LINUX_BACKING_DEV_H.
Counter record alloc_tag_counters holds two wide unsigned totals. One total tracks bytes charged. Other total tracks allocation calls. Separation allows per CPU updates with later summation.

Allocation tag alloc_tag pairs a code location descriptor with a pointer to per CPU counters and requires eight byte alignment. Kernel section record holds a pointer to the first tag plus a count. Module section record holds either a start address or a first tag pointer together with an end address and a used size.

Empty marker CODETAG_EMPTY is a distinguished non null address with value one, that is 1, signalling a deliberately cleared tag distinct from never set. With profiling available, emptiness test checks for that marker and the setter installs it when a reference holder exists.
Without profiling support, emptiness test is_codetag_empty always reports false and setter set_codetag_empty clears the stored pointer to null when a holder exists, so empty state is never observed.
Tag storage section name ALLOC_TAG_SECTION_NAME is 'alloc_tags'.
Delta record codetag_bytes pairs a code tag pointer with a signed byte adjustment for batched accounting transfer.
Helper ct_to_alloc_tag derives the enclosing allocation tag from a pointer to its embedded code descriptor using container address arithmetic.

Tag definition macro DEFINE_ALLOC_TAG creates a static aligned tag in the tag section initialized from the generic code tag initializer. Shared counter form points at a common counter. Null counter form leaves the pointer cleared. Per CPU form defines a dedicated per CPU counter beside the tag and points at it. Disabled form expands to nothing.

Profiling query mem_alloc_profiling_enabled consults a static branch default when available and always reports false when compiled out. Separate query mem_alloc_profiling_permanently_disabled reports true in the compiled out case.
Reader alloc_tag_read aggregates per CPU byte and call totals across all possible processors by resolving each CPU view of the tag counter pointer and accumulating into a zero started result.
Per CPU resolver per_cpu_ptr validates the pointer then either shifts by the CPU offset on multiprocessor builds or ignores the CPU index and returns the sole instance on single processor builds.

Debug check alloc_tag_add_check warns once if a reference still holds a prior non empty tag on add and warns once if the incoming tag is missing on add. Companion check alloc_tag_sub_check warns once if the reference lacks any tag on subtract. Stripped builds provide empty checks and an empty early page frame hook alloc_tag_add_early_pfn that accept the same arguments and do nothing.

Setter __alloc_tag_ref_set first runs the add check then fails when either holder or tag is missing, otherwise storing the address of the embedded code descriptor and reporting success. Counting wrapper alloc_tag_ref_set additionally increments the current CPU call total on success and reports failure without counting when the inner setter fails.

Charge operation alloc_tag_add attempts the counting reference install and only on success through the likely path adds the supplied byte size to the current CPU byte total. Disabled build provides an empty charge operation.

Release operation alloc_tag_sub runs the subtract check and returns when holder or stored pointer is missing. If the holder carries the empty marker it clears to null and returns without accounting. Otherwise it converts the code pointer to its tag, subtracts bytes and decrements calls on the current CPU, then clears the holder. Disabled build provides an empty release.

Current CPU increment this_cpu_inc acts as add of one. Current CPU add this_cpu_add routes through a size dispatched primitive. Current CPU subtract this_cpu_sub acts as add of a negated value with preserved type. Current CPU decrement this_cpu_dec acts as subtract of one.

Accuracy setter alloc_tag_set_inaccurate installs an inaccurate bit in the code descriptor flags. Tester alloc_tag_is_inaccurate reports whether that bit is present. Recording macro alloc_tag_record copies the current task allocation tag into a caller variable when enabled and does nothing when disabled, with matching empty setter and false tester in disabled builds.

Hook wrapper alloc_hooks_tag runs a supplied allocation expression directly when profiling is off, otherwise saving the current tag around the expression using a caller supplied tag and restoring the prior value afterwards, returning the expression result. Convenience form alloc_hooks defines a fresh tag at the call site then delegates to the tag form.

Writeback state word holds separate bits manipulated only with atomic bit operations. Registration completed is WB_registered. Active writeback is WB_writeback_running. Dirty IO presence is WB_has_dirty_io. All pages work is WB_start_all. Dontcache work is WB_start_dontcache.

Writeback counters use item identifiers. Reclaimable is WB_RECLAIMABLE. Under writeback is WB_WRITEBACK. Dirtied total is WB_DIRTIED. Written total is WB_WRITTEN. Dontcache dirty is WB_DONTCACHE_DIRTY. Array size is NR_WB_STAT_ITEMS. Batch threshold WB_STAT_BATCH grows with processor count via a logarithmic term scaled by eight, that is 8.

Writeback trigger reasons distinguish separate causes. Background is WB_REASON_BACKGROUND. Reclaim is WB_REASON_VMSCAN. Sync is WB_REASON_SYNC. Periodic is WB_REASON_PERIODIC. Filesystem free space is WB_REASON_FS_FREE_SPACE. Legacy forker thread is WB_REASON_FORKER_THREAD. Foreign flush is WB_REASON_FOREIGN_FLUSH. Dontcache is WB_REASON_DONTCACHE. Upper bound is WB_REASON_MAX.
Completion tracker wb_completion holds an atomic reference count plus a wait queue pointer and two jiffies stamps for slow progress detection and wait start.

Completion initializer __WB_COMPLETION_INIT sets the count to one, that is 1, and records the supplied queue. Device scoped initializer WB_COMPLETION_INIT binds the queue from the backing device. Defining macro DEFINE_WB_COMPLETION declares a local tracker initialized that way.

Per writeback context bdi_writeback anchors to its parent device info and carries a state word plus a last flush stamp. Four inode queues track dirty, IO, more IO and dirty time, with an atomic count of inodes under writeback and a per item statistics array. Bandwidth estimation keeps time and dirty and written stamps plus current and smoothed bandwidth, with base and balanced dirty throttling rates, local completion accounting, an exceeded flag and a start all reason. Scheduling uses delayed work for writeback and for bandwidth estimation, linked into the device list. Cgroup builds add a reference count for non root contexts, memory and block cgroup links with list nodes, an attached inode list, offline linkage, switching work with queued contexts, and a release work or RCU union.
Inode queues and attached list require the list spinlock named list_lock. Work list and delayed work scheduling require the work spinlock named work_lock. State word uses atomic bit operations.

Device info backing_dev_info carries a numeric identifier used as tree key with list linkage, readahead and IO sizes, a reference count, capability word and ratio limits. Total write bandwidth is an atomic long positive exactly when dirty contexts exist, plus a throttle sleep stamp. It embeds the root writeback context and the list of all contexts, with cgroup builds adding an active tree, a release mutex and a switch semaphore. It also holds a wait queue, device and owner pointers, a 64 character device name, and an optional debug entry. Lock cookie wb_lock_cookie pairs a boolean locked flag with saved interrupt flags.

With cgroup writeback, conditional acquire wb_tryget and acquire wb_get succeed immediately for the root context without counting, while non root contexts delegate to per CPU reference helpers. Batched release wb_put_many warns once and returns when the parent device pointer is missing, otherwise delegating non root releases to the per CPU helper. Single release wb_put delegates to batched release of one, that is 1. Dying query wb_dying delegates to the reference dying test.

Without cgroup writeback, conditional acquire wb_tryget always succeeds, acquire wb_get does nothing, single release wb_put does nothing, batched release wb_put_many does nothing, and dying query wb_dying always reports false, so only the root context exists.

Dying probe percpu_ref_is_dying inspects the dead mark on the stored pointer. Liveness probe __ref_is_percpu reads the counter pointer once and reports per CPU mode only when neither atomic nor dead marks are present, otherwise reporting atomic mode. Conditional acquire percpu_ref_tryget with many form percpu_ref_tryget_many and unconditional acquire percpu_ref_get with many form percpu_ref_get_many add to the current CPU counter in per CPU mode, otherwise using atomic long addition with a zero guard for the conditional form. Release percpu_ref_put_many subtracts from the current CPU counter in per CPU mode, otherwise atomically subtracts and invokes the release callback exactly when the count reaches zero.
Device acquire bdi_get increments its reference count and returns the same pointer to the caller.

Dirty presence wb_has_dirty_io tests the dedicated state bit on a context. Device dirty presence bdi_has_dirty_io reads total write bandwidth as a positive indicator. Statistics update wb_stat_mod adds a signed delta to the selected per CPU counter using the writeback batch threshold.

Batched addition percpu_counter_add_batch and generic addition percpu_counter_add route through each other with global or supplied batching on some builds, while a low level build updates the central count under interrupt save and restore. Positive read percpu_counter_read_positive clamps negative observations to zero, with one build using a single load and another using a direct load. Positive sum percpu_counter_sum_positive aggregates then clamps, with a simplified build delegating sum to the positive read.

Context read wb_stat returns the non negative current value for an item, while summed read wb_stat_sum returns the non negative aggregate across CPUs. Error bound wb_stat_error equals processor count scaled by the batch threshold on multiprocessor builds and one, that is 1, otherwise.
Ratio scale BDI_RATIO_SCALE equals 10000. Writeback capability BDI_CAP_WRITEBACK is the lowest capability bit. Strict limit BDI_CAP_STRICTLIMIT is the next capability bit.

Running test writeback_in_progress checks the dedicated running bit on the context. Mapping capability mapping_can_writeback derives from the owning device capability word testing the writeback bit. Dirty exceeded query bdi_wb_dirty_exceeded returns the root context exceeded flag. Inode statistics update bdi_wb_stat_mod routes to the root context of the owning device for the selected item.

Enablement test inode_cgwb_enabled requires default hierarchy for both memory and IO controllers, plus writeback capability on the owning device, plus the filesystem superblock carrying the cgroup writeback flag.

With cgroup support, lookup wb_find_current returns the root when the caller memory context lacks a parent, otherwise looking up the device tree by memory context identifier and returning the entry only when its block cgroup matches the caller block cgroup, else reporting missing. Without cgroup support, the same lookup always returns the root context.

Acquire wb_get_create_current first attempts a read side lookup with conditional reference acquisition, and when that yields nothing it obtains a caller memory reference, delegates creation or lookup to the device creator, releases the temporary reference, and returns the resulting context.
